- Primary concerns: predictable latency (p95 targets), isolation from noisy neighbors, and data controls for PII in logs.

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the clear recap — that matches our notes. Quick answers and clarifications below: 

1) Latency: p95 under 200ms for the majority of calls is a firm requirement for the user-facing search flow. For background/background batch jobs we can accept higher.
2) SLA: we're targeting a multi-region uptime SLA comparable to 99.9% for production. During pilot we can be more flexible.
3) Data residency: All production traffic must stay in US regions; we will need VPC peering or private link and assurances that control-plane metadata won't expose PII.
4) Pilot: we can scope a 2-week pilot with a representative peak of 250-300 reqs/s and avg payloads ~3-4KB.

Also, one other major ask from our infra team: can you share any performance isolation guarantees/approach for noisy neighbors? We want to avoid noisy-resource interference where other tenants on shared infra could spike latency for us.

Tom — looping you in to confirm availability next Wed (4/21) afternoon for a technical deep dive.

Regards,

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear answers. I wanted to address the noisy neighbor / isolation and SLO questions you raised and propose a couple pragmatic options for pilot vs production: 

Options (short):
- Hosted API (shared): fastest to get started, but shared pools can see performance variability under contention. We mitigate with autoscaling and prefix/KV caching, but there is residual cross-tenant variance — not recommended if you require strict p95 guarantees.

- Dedicated Capacity (recommended for FinPay): reserved GPU pools (customer-dedicated min capacity) with no other tenants on those nodes. Provides predictable throughput & much tighter latency distribution. We offer:
  * Reserved GPU pools mapped to your workload (you control model pins / versions).
  * VPC peering or PrivateLink for data plane; control plane can be configured as private if needed (Private deployment add-on).
  * Autoscaling policies with warm standby nodes to avoid cold-start latency spikes during short peaks.

- Private VPC / On-prem: full isolation and control plane in your VPC or on-prem; recommended when compliance or data residency requires it. Longer lead time and higher operational overhead.

Noisy neighbor mitigation details (how Dedicated helps):
- Dedicated pools ensure no other customer processes are scheduled on the same GPUs — that eliminates GPU contention.
- We isolate network egress/ingress via VPC peering segments and limit noisy-egress interference.
- For shared pools we use continuous-batching scheduling & fairness windows, but some tail variability can remain.

SLO / SLA notes:
- Pilot: we can confirm p95 ~200-300ms for a pilot with two x A100 nodes depending on model size and prompt profiles.
- Production Dedicated SLA: we offer an SLA target we can include in the MSA; typical target for Dedicated customers with committed capacity is 99.9% uptime and p95 latency commitments tailored to the workload in the SLO appendix. Specific numeric p95 guarantees require sizing & workload validation during pilot.

Recommended next steps (practical):
1) Pilot deployment on Dedicated capacity with 2x A100 shaping nodes + warm standby. We'll run your peak load profile (250-300 reqs/s) for 2 weeks and measure p95/99 latencies.
2) During the pilot we'll provide a perf runbook and automated traces for tail-latency analysis.
3) Post-pilot we'll produce an SLO appendix that can be added to the MSA with numeric p95 targets based on pilot results.

I've attached a short technical brief (dedicated-capacity-technical-brief.pdf) with sizing guidance and example autoscale configs. Happy to go through this with Tom on Wed 4/21 — Priyom, please select a slot and I'll join.

Marissa
